complexity_scope.guarantee: Worst-case deterministic budget-and-output guarantee for every legal f and fixed Oracle selection. Lower witness is existential for each algorithm; no probability convention is introduced.

complexity_scope.oracle: Exact paired value plus full globally supporting Riemannian subgradient from one fixed selection for one globally defined f.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Any ambient output xhat; objective gap <=epsilon LR. Hard witness yields gap >=2epsilon LR, including unqueried outputs.
complexity_scope.regime: R,L>0; matching range 0<epsilon<=1/64; dimension supremum over d>=2; hard d=T+2.

complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Lower: every deterministic adaptive algorithm, with unrestricted ambient queries and output. Upper: projected exponential subgradient steps followed by best observed value selection.

content.intended_use: Match the projected-subgradient upper rate with an unrestricted deterministic lower bound, including arbitrary unqueried outputs.

map: Lemma5.1 supplies joint distance convexity and log contraction. Lemma5.2 proves every global convex L-Lipschitz objective has nonempty compact convex subdifferentials with unique minimum-norm selections. Lemmas5.3–5.4 give a global carrier objective and an exact value/full-subgradient contact certificate.

P103 Eq.(7), Lemmas25–26 provide nested candidate spheres and common projection geometry. Only that geometry is imported; P103 A1/A2 hardness and its budget constants are not used as unrestricted hardness. Primary §6 expresses the geometry as p=cosh S c+sinh S v, with D=arcosh(cosh S cosh dist(c,z)), a=sinh D/sinh S and u=u_V+v/a.

Lemma6.1 is the Lorentz halfspace–ball criterion. Lemmas6.2–6.3 prove persistence of F_theta(a)=((theta-mu)a+mu/a)/sqrt(1+mu^2-2mu theta-mu^2/a^2): its reference-angle square identity and single-turning-point argument control every later a', rather than only the current value.

Lemmas6.4–6.5 turn containment of the current public ball, sinh r_S=eta tanh S, into normal reserve -a<n_V,u_V>>=eta||n_V||, and select candidate-independent minimizing contacts. On-domain queries use q_V=-mu u_V and beta=sqrt(1-mu^2||u_V||^2).

Proposition6.6 retains residual latitude <e,v>=-eta when beta>0; if beta=0 it makes no cut. It proves mu<theta<=1 and F_theta(a')>=eta for every a'>=a, handling a>=a0, strict interior a<a0, and beta=0 separately. Proposition6.7 projects the same physical archived normal into every later public Lorentz subspace and applies Lemma6.1 to contain every future public ball.

§7.1 initializes W=span{o}, V=P={o}, c=o, S=R. Each new query chooses its contact over P, cuts by at most one residual direction, installs a new intrinsic ball and retains the closed convex hull of all historical public balls. Cached queries and beta=0 queries leave the state unchanged. Residual dimension d-t>=2 makes each required latitude nonempty.

Proposition7.1 proves nested physical candidates, compact public domains and public archived contacts/directions. Every archived normal n_i,p=q_i+mu(p-cosh D_i z_i)/sinh D_i contains the entire evolving P and p. Thus K=closed gconv(P union {p}) supports all archived contacts simultaneously; Lemmas5.3–5.4 realize every archived exact value and full selected vector using one F_{K,p}. Remark7.2 preserves strict separation of old exterior queries even after their directions become public.

If k_t is the number of actual cuts, sinh S_t=sigma^{k_t}sinh R. For t<=T, k_t(-log sigma)<=log(2cosh(R/2))=log(sinh R/sinh(R/2)), so S_t>=R/2. For arbitrary final xhat choose a surviving unit residual v with <v,xhat>_L<=0; then dist(xhat,p)>=S_t and F_{K,p}(xhat)>=mu S_t>=2epsilon R.

Fix that final F and use cached subgradients at queried points, minimum-norm selections elsewhere. Deterministic replay gives the same transcript and failed output against this single fixed Oracle. If the simulation requests call T+1, fix any completion at prefix T to witness budget failure; if it stalls at a finite prefix, fix that prefix completion to witness nonreturn.

§7.4 has eta^2=64epsilon^2/(1-16epsilon^2)^2<=65epsilon^2<1/2 and -log sigma<=eta^2. Also zeta_R<=R+1 and log(2cosh(R/2))>=zeta_R/4. Hence T+1>log(2cosh(R/2))/(-log sigma)>=zeta_R/(260epsilon^2). Multiplying all public answers and the final objective by L preserves the simulation even when A adapts to their scale.

map: Let p minimize f in the closed localization ball; N=ceil(zeta_{3R}/epsilon^2), alpha=R/(L sqrt(zeta_{3R}N)), x0=o. Query x_j and set y_j=exp_{x_j}(-alpha g_j), x_{j+1}=projection onto closed B(o,R) of y_j, j=0,...,N-1. Return the queried point with least observed value; no minimum value is required.

Global support plus Lipschitzness gives ||g_j||<=L. Since alpha L<=R, each unprojected segment is within 3R of p. The Hessian of dist(.,p)^2/2 has eigenvalues 1 and r coth r, bounded above by zeta_{3R} on that segment.

Taylor and support imply dist(y_j,p)^2<=dist(x_j,p)^2-2alpha(f(x_j)-f(p))+zeta_{3R}alpha^2 L^2. Projection does not increase distance to p: projection optimality and the lower Hessian bound I give the squared-distance Pythagorean inequality.
Sum the recursion and use dist(o,p)^2<=R^2 to obtain best gap <=R^2/(2alpha N)+zeta_{3R}alpha L^2/2=LR sqrt(zeta_{3R}/N)<=epsilon LR. Finally tanh(3R)>=tanh R implies zeta_{3R}<=3zeta_R.

proofs.full_local_argument: Set R0=3R/4 and use the Theorem3.1 hard witness with the same epsilon,L. Its minimizer has dist(o,p)=R0<R, and its output gap is at least 2epsilon LR0=(3/2)epsilon LR>epsilon LR, so it is also a failure witness for the open-ball task at radius R. Since tanh R0<=tanh R, zeta_R0=R0/tanh R0>=(3/4)R/tanh R=(3/4)zeta_R. The budget calibration at R0 therefore gives lower bound zeta_R0/(260epsilon^2)>=3zeta_R/(1040epsilon^2). The open-ball class is contained in the closed-ball class, so the same upper algorithm gives ceil(3zeta_R/epsilon^2).

assumptions: o,d,R,L,epsilon and the ambient hyperbolic geometry are known.
Queries may be arbitrary ambient points, including outside the localization ball, prior geodesic spans and historical supporting halfspaces.
A call returns both an exact value and the entire selected globally supporting tangent subgradient. The upper guarantee must hold for every legal fixed selection.
Algorithms are deterministic, with arbitrary internal computation and exact geometric operations free of objective-Oracle charges. Output may be any ambient point, whether queried or not.
statement.conclusion: zeta_R/(260epsilon^2)<=Q*(R,epsilon)<=ceil(3zeta_R/epsilon^2), with universal constants. In each d, Q*_d<=ceil(zeta_{3R}/epsilon^2)<=ceil(3zeta_R/epsilon^2). If localization instead requires a minimizer in the open ball B(o,R), the dimension-uniform complexity is at least 3zeta_R/(1040epsilon^2) and at most ceil(3zeta_R/epsilon^2).
statement.objects_and_definitions: H^d has sectional curvature -1. F_d(R,L) is the set of globally geodesically convex f:H^d->R with |f(x)-f(y)|<=L dist(x,y) for all x,y and argmin f intersect closed B(o,R) nonempty. Define partial f(x)={g in T_x H^d: f(y)>=f(x)+<g,log_x y> for every y}. O(f) consists of fixed maps O_f(x)=(f(x),g_f(x)), g_f(x) in partial f(x). For deterministic A, N_A counts paired calls before returning xhat, and is infinity if A never returns. Q*_d(R,epsilon)=inf{N in nonnegative integers: exists A, for every f in F_d(R,L) and every O_f in O(f), N_A<=N and f(xhat)-min f<=epsilon LR}; an empty feasible set has infimum infinity. Q*(R,epsilon)=sup_{d>=2}Q*_d(R,epsilon), and zeta_R=R/tanh R. Scaling values and vectors shows Q* is independent of L.
statement.parameter_domains: d>=2 integer for the upper bound; R,L>0; 0<epsilon<=1/64 for matching bounds. Proposition8.1 upper bound separately holds for 0<epsilon<1. The hard dimension is d=T+2, not an arbitrary prescribed fixed dimension.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every R,L>0 and 0<epsilon<=1/64 the dimension supremum satisfies the stated bounds. More precisely, with mu=4epsilon, eta=2mu/(1-mu^2), sigma=sqrt(1-eta^2), T=floor(log(2cosh(R/2))/(-log sigma)) and d=T+2, every deterministic algorithm returning after at most T calls has a witness consisting of one fixed f in F_d(R,L) with a unique global minimizer and one fixed legal O_f, for which its output gap is at least 2epsilon LR. No randomized-algorithm claim.
